result:
I built the protocol audit tool (`tools/release/protocol-audit.mjs`) and ran it over DG0–DG6. The real run exits 1: it found 248 historic hits, all in DG0–DG6, and none in DG7. I did not fix or rewrite any record (D-243 Q13). The run took 2.97 s across 697 runs, 686 assignments, 96 committed versions of `progress.md` and 221 findings. The handback is `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-I-devops-engineer.md`.

**The tool.** Read-only, Node built-ins only, with `--stage DGx` (repeatable) or `--all`. It writes a JSON report and a short summary, and exits 0 when clean, 1 on a hit and 2 when it cannot run (BLOCKED). It has nine checks, each mapped to its requirement clause:

| Check | Requirement | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | REQ-DLV-009 | at most four concurrent runs per gate |
| C2 | REQ-DLV-011 | all ten assignment contract elements, named in the tool and the test |
| C3 | REQ-DLV-012 | the five handback sections |
| C4 | REQ-DLV-008 | no file shared by concurrent assignments (declared and actually written) |
| C5 | REQ-DLV-024 | `--historical` logged in test-evidence before the first implementation run |
| C6 | REQ-DLV-028, REQ-DLV-012 | the six gate-update elements; no task with open gaps reported complete |
| C7 | REQ-DLV-018 | three failed fixes produce a blocker entry |
| C8 | REQ-DLV-027 | approval-claim scan, including any text equating product G6 with DG7 |
| C9 | REQ-DLV-027 / REQ-DLV-040 | stage order; F-DG6-952 is reported as its accepted observation, not a new hit |

C2, C3, C6 and C8 read prose with patterns, so some hits may be phrasings the patterns miss. Every hit carries the matched text or the missing items for a human to judge.

**Checks run, all exit 0:**
- **Fixture tests:** 25/25 pass. Each of the 11 seeded violations is caught by its own check, with every other check passing.
- **`pnpm lint`:** passes, but the repository's ESLint config ignores `tools/release/**`, so it doesn't lint these files. ESLint with `--no-ignore` on both files also exits 0.
- **Prettier check over all files:** passes.
- **`validate.mjs --historical --stage DG6`:** passes.

**Main historic hits (my proposed class in brackets; you decide):**
- **Five concurrent runs:** twice in DG5 (2026-10-17) and once in DG6 (2026-11-01), with no disclosure in `decisions.md`. DG6 also has 31 run directories with no `meta.json`, so its true peak is unknown. [observation]
- **`--historical` evidence:** in DG1–DG6, no log in test-evidence is dated before the first implementation run, but each stage's ARCH handback written before that run states it. [closable by an added record: copy the logs in]
- **F-DG3-100:** four failed fix verifications and no blocker entry with a recovery plan; DG3 was approved anyway. [observation, or a reopen question for the user]
- **DG6 gate update in `progress.md`:** it lacks the "capabilities demonstrated" element. [closable by an added note]
- **Shared files:** concurrent assignments declared the same files (mostly the append-only `platform/db-errors.ts` and `schemas/index.ts`), but no two concurrent runs actually wrote the same file in any gate. 22 of the 24 DG4 pairs come from tasks citing a whole work-split section, so they overstate the overlap. [observation]
- **Incomplete assignments:** some assignments miss contract elements, most often dependency status and permitted files; 49 of 100 are flagged in DG0, dropping to 6 of 125 in DG5. [observation]
- **Handback sections:** 48 implementation handbacks miss one of the five sections by heading. [observation]
- **One changed assignment:** `T-DG6-FE-Z3.md` changed after its run, and no committed version matches the hash the run recorded. [observation, or a note]
- **Approval claims:** none found. My first draft had 36 hits, all negated disclaimers, which the final rule allows.

**Decisions for you:**
- Whether REQ-DLV-009 can be marked IMPLEMENTED at DG7 given the DG5 and DG6 overlaps above four.
- Whether the F-DG3-100 case means DG3 needs reopening.
- Whether shared append-only files count as "sharing a writable file" under REQ-DLV-008.
- Whether the original `--historical` outputs still exist anywhere to copy in; if not, the handback statements are the only evidence.

The full `--all` run exits 1 on these historic records by design, so it shouldn't be a blocking CI step until you decide how to treat them. Only the fixture tests are suitable for CI now.

Files are in `/home/user/My-owns`:
- `tools/release/protocol-audit.mjs`
- `tools/release/tests/protocol-audit.test.mjs`
- `tools/release/tests/fixtures/protocol/`
- `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-I-devops-engineer.md`
- `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-I-evidence/` (the reports, plus `final-checks.log` with every command output and checksum)
